comparator.name: Computing Science (Informatica)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current UvA curriculum page gives two 60-EC compulsory years. Year 1 combines programming, computer architecture, data structures, web technology, programming languages, discrete mathematics and logic, linear algebra, operating systems, Internet of Things and two academic-skills components. Year 2 adds databases, networks and security, distributed and parallel programming, statistics, a numerical project, algorithms and complexity, computer vision, automata and formal languages, reflection on digital society, software engineering and two academic-skills components. Year 3 contains 30 EC of genuine open elective space, a 12-EC restricted choice of two out of three named courses, and an 18-EC bachelor project. Compiler Construction and Classical Cryptography are selected as the first two officially listed restricted choices; Theory of Functional Programming is not combined with them. The overview confirms a Dutch-taught, full-time 180-EC BSc under RIO code 56978.

alternatives.label: Computer systems, software and algorithms
alternatives.concept: Builds a UCR computing programme around programming, networks and operating systems, databases, software development, algorithms and mathematical foundations, with data and AI applications. UCR covers substantial computer-science content but has less structured hardware, security, parallel-systems and formal research training than UvA.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed schedule preserves a substantial software-and-systems strand alongside algorithms, discrete mathematics, statistics, data science and machine learning.
progression: Six four-course semesters in 2026–29, with PPD in Year 1 and at least six 300-level courses. The enriched UCR workbook confirms offerings and all formal prerequisites in earlier semesters; programming and mathematical gates precede advanced computing and AI.

alternatives.label: Mathematical computing and intelligent systems
alternatives.concept: Uses the same programming and systems foundation, then emphasizes numerical methods, linear systems, calculus, optimization, machine learning, robotics and human-centred AI. This is a mathematical and modelling direction within computing rather than a claim to reproduce UvA's full systems curriculum.
alternatives.labelReason: Advanced mathematics and robotics replace part of the software-development and algorithms sequence while retaining foundational computer science.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses change: Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Linear Systems, Advanced Calculus and Robotics replace Consumer Product Design, Software Development, Advanced Algorithms and Ethics. The resulting 30 EC shift emphasizes mathematical modelling and intelligent systems.
progression: Six four-course semesters in 2026–29, with PPD in Year 1 and at least six 300-level courses. The enriched UCR workbook confirms offerings and all formal prerequisites in earlier semesters; programming and mathematical gates precede advanced computing and AI.

selection.assessment: The closest programme and a 30-EC-distinct mathematical and intelligent-systems direction are feasible. All remaining generator-eligible interests concern the same computer-science core, software and systems emphasis, or are already represented by these two programmes. Curricular topics such as graphics, games, security and human-computer interaction strengthen the map but cannot independently generate a third alternative, and UCR does not offer a coherent specialist sequence in those areas.

notes.text: The UvA degree requires computer architecture, web technology, programming languages, operating systems, Internet of Things, networks and security, distributed and parallel programming, automata and formal languages, a software-engineering project, selected compiler construction and cryptography, and an 18-EC final project. UCR can build a substantial programme in programming, databases, networks and operating systems, algorithms, mathematics, data science and AI, but it does not reproduce this complete structured systems and research sequence.
